stem: A liver transplant recipient with cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection develops cholestatic laboratory abnormalities. Which CMV-related allograft complication should the coordinator recognize?

explanation.rationale_correct: Organ-specific CMV effects on allografts include vanishing bile duct syndrome in liver transplants, which may present with cholestatic injury patterns.

rationale_incorrect.B: Bronchiolitis obliterans is the listed CMV organ-specific effect for lung rather than liver allografts.
rationale_incorrect.C: Coronary artery vasculopathy is the listed CMV organ-specific effect for heart allografts.
rationale_incorrect.D: Glomerulopathy is the listed CMV organ-specific kidney effect rather than the primary liver biliary complication.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → CMV → 8. Organ-specific effects on allograft → a.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → CMV → 8. Organ-specific effects on allograft → a. (liver: vanishing bile duct syndrome); PDF p. 202 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Liver CMV vanishing-bile-duct angle distinct from cholangitis/ERCP management (cctc-3039) and metabolic bone disease (cctc-3058); anchor verified on Cupples p. 202.

stem: When monitoring a kidney transplant recipient with recurrent cytomegalovirus (CMV) replication, which long-term allograft complication is associated with CMV in standard references?

explanation.rationale_correct: Organ-specific CMV effects on allografts include glomerulopathy in kidney transplant recipients.

rationale_incorrect.B: Vanishing bile duct syndrome is the listed CMV organ-specific effect for liver allografts.
rationale_incorrect.C: Bronchiolitis obliterans is the listed CMV organ-specific effect for lung allografts.
rationale_incorrect.D: Oral aversion is an intestine transplant feeding complication unrelated to CMV kidney effects.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → CMV → 8. Organ-specific effects on allograft → d.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → CMV → 8. Organ-specific effects on allograft → d. (kidney: glomerulopathy); PDF p. 202 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Kidney CMV glomerulopathy angle distinct from heart CAV/LV dysfunction (cctc-3066) and skin-cancer long-term risk (cctc-3055); anchor verified on Cupples p. 202.

stem: An adult kidney transplant recipient has delayed graft function attributed to acute tubular necrosis (ATN) without rejection or obstruction. Evaluate the following clinical statements:

elements.text: Increased blood urea nitrogen and creatinine may be present.
Pulmonary edema is a characteristic isolated sign that always distinguishes ATN from other causes.
Elevated potassium and magnesium levels may occur.

explanation.rationale_correct: ATN presents as renal failure in the absence of rejection or obstruction with increased BUN/creatinine, anuria or oliguria, and elevated potassium and magnesium. Pulmonary edema is not listed among the characteristic ATN signs in the source question set.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—elevated potassium and magnesium are listed ATN signs.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III overstates pulmonary edema as a distinguishing isolated ATN sign.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false as stated—pulmonary edema is not among the listed characteristic ATN signs.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Kidney Transplantation → review questions → ATN signs → 5.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: ATN presents as renal failure … Increased BUN and creatinine … Anuria or oliguria … Elevated potassium and magnesium levels

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 7 → review questions → ATN signs → 5. (increased BUN/creatinine, oliguria/anuria, elevated potassium/magnesium); PDF p. 819–820 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Synthesized item. Eighteenth complex_combo in bank; adult ATN signs angle distinct from pediatric ATN monitoring combo (cctc-3067) and ureteral obstruction (cctc-3047); answer key verified on Cupples p. 820 (1, 2, 4).

stem: When counseling a kidney recipient starting belatacept maintenance therapy, which medication-safety point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease is an adverse effect and EBV IgG seropositivity is required before use
Belatacept requires daily trough level monitoring like tacrolimus
Belatacept is safe in all Epstein-Barr virus–seronegative recipients without added risk
Belatacept replaces the need for infection monitoring after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Belatacept adverse effects include posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease, and recipients must be Epstein-Barr virus IgG seropositive to decrease PTLD risk; belatacept does not require therapeutic drug level monitoring.

rationale_incorrect.B: No belatacept level monitoring is necessary per standard references.
rationale_incorrect.C: EBV-seronegative recipients have higher PTLD risk; seropositivity is required before belatacept use.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recipients still require post-transplant infection and complication monitoring while on belatacept.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: seropositive for Epstein-Barr virus IgG to decrease the risk of developing PTLD … PTLD … No monitoring of levels are necessary

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 4 → Belatacept → 3.c. and 4.e. (EBV IgG seropositivity required; PTLD adverse effect; no level monitoring); PDF p. 157 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Belatacept post-transplant counseling paired with pretransplant eligibility item (cctc-2070); distinct from tacrolimus tremor (cctc-3052) and cyclosporine cosmetic effects (cctc-3044); anchor verified on Cupples p. 157.
